title: Postpartum Depression Screening Across Languages
summary: Build multilingual postpartum depression screening with validated tools, qualified interpretation, risk review, and closed-loop referrals.
body_markdown:
###


No. Use an approved, validated language version with its scoring instructions. Ad hoc translation can change item meaning, response choices, and the validity of the score.


###


No. It indicates that the patient needs clinical assessment. The response plan should address urgency, diagnostic evaluation, treatment options, monitoring, and follow-up.


###


The responsible clinician should immediately assess risk under the organization’s protocol and arrange risk-tailored management. Keep qualified language support available throughout the process.


###


Yes. Pediatric practices can screen at recommended well-infant visits when they have procedures for referral, communication with maternal care, urgent response, and follow-up.


###


Measure correct language-version use, completed screens, immediate safety reviews, referral scheduling, referral completion, failed language support, and unresolved follow-up by setting and language.
